ai.title: process-str-replace allowMultiple match fix
ai.summary: process-str-replace.ts returns original oldStr when allowMultiple=true with count > 1, bypassing indentation-aware retry. Fixes unit test failures in process-str-replace.test.ts. Scope limited to backend string replacement utility.

eli5.text: When the system replaces text in multiple places at once, it now correctly recognizes that this is intentional and skips the usual safety check that asks for a more specific search term. Previously, asking to replace the same word in several spots would fail with an error suggesting there was ambiguity, even when multiple replacements were explicitly allowed. You would have noticed this as an unexpected error message when bulk-updating repetitive text, which no longer happens.

ai.title: Fix unit tests
ai.summary: Updated assertions in `process-str-replace.test.ts` to match actual message array structure and formatting. Replaced loose string checks with strict length and index validation for multi-occurrence errors. Adjusted quote styles and line breaks to satisfy linter rules.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team tightened up some automated checks that make sure the search-and-replace feature works correctly. These checks now look more carefully at the specific warning messages the system gives you when text appears multiple times. If you were watching the code health dashboard, you might notice fewer false alerts about these checks.

ai.title: Inline agent inherits onReponseChunk
ai.summary: Inline agent execution now passes parent's writeToClient to child's onResponseChunk, removing no-op handler and expireMessages import. Handler signature updated to accept string | PrintModeEvent chunks. Scope: backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts, backend/src/tools/handlers/handler-function-type.ts, backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-inline.ts.

eli5.text: When you run a helper assistant inside your main assistant (an inline sub-agent), the helper now sends its streaming output straight to the same place the main assistant sends its text, instead of quietly swallowing it. The helper no longer comes with a do-nothing handler or the unused message-expiry code it was pulling in, and the spot that hands out the parent's output destination was updated so it accepts the helper's mixed text and structured-event chunks. If you watched a conversation that spawns an inline helper, you would now see the helper's words appear in real time alongside the parent's, rather than the helper's output vanishing into a handler that did nothing.

ai.title: Add writeToClient stub to spawn agent tests
ai.summary: Added writeToClient: () => {} to mock contexts in backend/src/__tests__/spawn-agents-permissions.test.ts. Fixes type errors for handleSpawnAgentInline. Internal test refactor.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team adjusted how they write and run automated checks for a part of the app that starts helper agents. These checks now include a tiny placeholder action that previous validations were missing, which resolves the errors the team noticed when assembling these mock scenarios. Nothing changes for you today, this only cleans up the internal testing setup so future changes to how helpers are spawned can be verified reliably. If you peeked at the test files, you'd just see some formatting tightened and that missing placeholder action added to the mock setups.

Typing certain words triggers animated celebrations: confetti bursts of code symbols and emojis, a cascading green-code rain effect, and a slow typewriter-style message reveal. A new digital assistant named Chloe has also been added to help create such fun features. These additions are documented in a guide for the team.

eli5.text: The glitchy terminal text now plays its animation reliably when the page loads, instead of occasionally stuttering or misbehaving. The small bug fix cleaned up a behind-the-scenes timing detail in the animation logic; visually, the text flicker you see on the main terminal screen will just work as intended with no noticeable difference unless you were hitting the rare glitch. No new features were added, this is live today as a stability tidy-up for the existing terminal display.

ai.title: Add stepsComplete signal to handleSteps generator protocol
ai.summary: The `handleSteps` generator protocol now receives a `stepsComplete` boolean in the yield return value, allowing agent loops to break cleanly when the step limit is reached. Previously, hitting `stepsRemaining <= 0` would inject a system message and end the turn, but the generator state remained active; now, `runProgrammaticStep` propagates this flag, and built-in agents like `base.ts` and `thinking-base.ts` check it to exit their `while(true)` loops. The `STEP_ALL` mode is also refactored from a special generator value to a separate `agentIdToStepAll` set, enabling `stepsComplete` to clear that state and resume normal stepping. Additionally, `StrReplaceParams` gains an optional `allowMultiple` flag for batch replacements.

eli5.text: When an AI assistant that can take multiple steps (like reading several files or making several edits) reaches its limit, it now stops cleanly instead of getting stuck in a loop. The system now tracks a 'steps complete' flag that lets these multi-step agents know when they've hit their step cap, so they can break out of their work loop gracefully. This affects the built-in agent types that handle complex tasks, and while you wouldn't see a visual change, the assistant will stop more reliably when it runs out of allowed steps instead of potentially continuing or behaving unpredictably.
